hints: Focus on what reacting with alkaline aqueous iodine tells you about the alcohol structure.
The positive iodoform test needs a CH3CH(OH) group, so check which options contain this unit and discard the others.
For the remaining alcohols, count dehydration products carefully, remembering that E/Z stereoisomers of an alkene count as two different alkenes.
walkthrough:
**Use the iodoform test to find the functional group**

A positive test with alkaline aqueous iodine means a yellow precipitate of CHI3. For an alcohol of formula C5H12O, this requires the group $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$.

**Eliminate options that cannot give iodoform**

Option A is a primary alcohol $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ with no $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ unit, so it is negative.

Option B is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)}-$, the OH carbon is attached to $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ not $\text{CH}_3$, so it is also negative.

This leaves only the two pentan-2-ol type structures:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}- \text{ group present}$$

**Count dehydration alkenes including stereoisomers**

Dehydration removes H2O by removing OH and a H from an adjacent carbon. Each different structural alkene counts, and E/Z isomers count separately.

For D, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$:
$$\text{pent-1-ene (1) + E-pent-2-ene + Z-pent-2-ene = 3 alkenes}$$
So D gives three alkenes, not two.

**Check the branched isomer**

For C, $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCH(OH)CH}_3$ (3-methylbutan-2-ol), OH is on C2.

Remove H from C1 gives:
$$\text{CH}_2\text{=CHCH(CH}_3\text{)}_2 \text{ (3-methylbut-1-ene) }$$
Remove H from C3 gives:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH=C(CH}_3\text{)}_2 \text{ (2-methylbut-2-ene) }$$
Neither shows E/Z isomerism, so this is two alkenes only. This matches both conditions.

options.A: CH3CH2CH(CH3)CH2OH is 2-methylbutan-1-ol, a primary alcohol. It lacks the CH3CH(OH) group needed for the iodoform reaction, so it will not react with alkaline aqueous iodine.
options.B: CH3CH2CH(OH)CH2CH3 is pentan-3-ol. Although it is a secondary alcohol, the carbon bearing OH is joined to two CH2CH3 groups, not to a CH3 group. It has no CH3CH(OH) unit, so the iodoform test is negative.
options.C: (CH3)2CHCH(OH)CH3 is 3-methylbutan-2-ol. It contains CH3CH(OH), so gives a positive iodoform test. Dehydration gives only 3-methylbut-1-ene and 2-methylbut-2-ene, two alkenes with no E/Z duplication, matching the question perfectly.
options.D: CH3CH2CH2CH(OH)CH3 is pentan-2-ol and does give a positive iodoform test. However dehydration gives pent-1-ene plus both E- and Z-pent-2-ene, which is three alkenes when stereoisomerism is counted, so it fails the 'two alkenes only' condition.
